caseno: Death Reference No.78 of 2014 with Criminal Appeal No.3378 of 2015
lawyer:
Md Aminul Islam DAG with Shamsunnahar (Laizu) and Farhana Afroze, AAGs—For the State. 

Hasna Begum, Advocate—For the State Defence. 

None appears—For the Appellant.
parties:
State ---- Petitioner
VS
Md Shafiqur Rahman @Shafique (absconding) ----- Condemned-Convict
full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker J : This reference under section 374 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been made by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Sylhet for confirmation of the sentence of death passed on the condemned-convict namely Md Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique (absconding) in Sessions Case No.1808 of 2013 (previous Sessions Case No.736 of 2012) arising out of Kotwali Model Police Station Case No.88, dated 30-11-2010 corresponding to GR Case No.1164 of 2010 under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. 

2. The co-accused of this case Sumon @ Mama Sumon against whom the learned Sessions Judge awarded lifelong imprisonment with a fine of Taka 10,000 (Ten thousand) in default to pay the fine, additional imprisonment for a term of two months under the above mentioned sections of the Penal Code, has filed a criminal appeal being No.3378 of 2015. 

3. The Death Reference and the aforesaid Appeal have been heard together and are being disposed of by this single judgment. 

4. The prosecution case as made out in the ejahar in a nutshell can be stated thus: 
One Haji Md Khorshed Ali, son of late Md Abdul Motaleb of village 12/A, Kumarpara, Ward No.18, Kotwali police station under Sylhet District lodged the First Information Report (FIR) with Kotwali Model Police Station before the Officer-in-Charge on 30-11-2010contending inter alia that the informant is the proprietor of Hotel Anurag situated at Dhupa Dighir Uttarpar of Sylhet town, and he was an immigrant of United Kingdom. Due to his old age with different diseases he returned back to this country and as a proprietor of the above mentioned Hotel started the same. The further case of the informant is such that his son the victim of this case, Atiqur Rahman @ Atique used to reside in London and prior to three years of the occurrence, the informant asked him to come back and the deceased Atiqur Rahman @ Atique after his return to this country was entrusted to supervise and manage the Hotel 'Anurag'. The deceased Atiqur Rahman @ Atique got him introduced with the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman Shafiq through one Mosharaff, a businessman of Latif Centre, Sylhet. The condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman was a businessman of VCD and DVD, and he used to sale the same to the deceased Atiqur Rahman and that the condemned-convict Shafique used to come to the deceased very often and stayed in his hotel as a boarder. On 23-11-2010 the convict Shafiqur Rahman hired the room No.322 of that hotel, identifying him as a son of one Hajee Rahmat Ullah and Shahebjadi Begum, and he stayed there until the date of occurrence i.e. up to 29-11- 2010. On the date of occurrence at about 3-00 pm at the request of the convict Shafiqur Rahman the deceased Atiqur Rahman @ Atique returned back to the hotel Anurag and went to the room No.322. After some time of his arrival in the said place of occurrence room, the convict Shafiqur Rahman and his two accomplices while where leaving the hotel, the Managers of that Hotel namely Salauddin and Shahabuddin asked the convict Shafiqur Rahman and his two accomplices as to where they are going. In reply to that, they told to the Managers that, for collecting money from SA Paribahan they are going outside. Subsequently, the General Manager of the hotel namely Mahmud-uz-zaman Jewel finding the mobile phone of the deceased Atiqur Rahman stopped, along with 4/5 employees of that hotel started to look after Atiqur Rahman, who was their junior boss and at a stage of searching, they went in front of room No.322 and hearing sound of water falling inside the said room No.322 which was under lock and key, with the help of duplicate key they opened the room, and found the deceased Atiqur Rahman @ Atique fastened by a rope in his legs, hands, neck and waist and the mouth of the deceased Atique at that time was closed by a scotch tape. Finding that condition of the deceased Atique, the General Manager told the driver of the deceased namely Alamgir to bring the informant Hajee Md Khorshed Ali from his residence. The General Manager informed the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) and police requesting them to come to the place of occurrence. Subsequently, the informant along with his wife and the deceased's wife coming to the hotel found the victim Atiqur Rahman @ Atique in the aforesaid condition and became senseless. After some time, the members of RAB and police force coming to the place of occurrence found the deceased and the police seized a Tiger Energy drink bottle from the place of occurrence room having some poisonous substance therein. They also seized some CD and VCD which were scattered inside the room. The mobile phone set and money bag of the deceased were missing, but the wristwatch of the deceased was on the floor of that room. The further case of the informant is such that the body of his son Atique was sent to Sylhet Osmani Medical College Hospital, from where he was declared 'dead'. Subsequently, the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique made a mobile phone call from his mobile phone No. '0175206307' to other mobile phone of the deceased Atique at 01.20 a.m. being No. '01746065732' and that phone call was received by the paternal father-in-law of the deceased namely Badrul Islam. The convict Shafiqur Rahman by that phone call wanted to know the condition of Atique, disclosing his identity as a friend of Atique. The phone number which was used by the condemned-convict Sofique was known to the hotel boy Mizan, inasmuch as in that phone number prior to the occurrence, Sofique requested the hotel boy Mizan on different occasions to give flexi load from outside of the hotel. 

5. Subsequently, after getting First Information Report, investigation was started by the concerned Kotwali Police Station, Sylhet and one Sub-Inspector Md Khasrul Alam Badal and Sub-inspector Md Abdul Alim were entrusted to investigate the case. During investigation the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman Shafique was arrested and he confessed his guilt in killing the deceased Atikur Rahman @ Atik before a Magistrate, 1st Class and his confessional statement was recorded by the learned Magistrate under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. After was closed, the investigation, the investigating officer finding prima-facie ingredients of the commission of offence against the convicted accused, namely Shafiqur Rahman Shafique and his accomplices Sumon @ Mama Sumon and Khokon, submitted charge sheet No.445 dated 18-6-2011 under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. 

6. While the case was ready for trial, it was sent to the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Sylhet. The learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge after framing charge on 11-9-2012 under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code read over and explained the same to the presentee accused persons Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique and Sumon @ Mama Sumon, who pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The other convicted person Khokon having been absconded, the charge was not possible to read over and explain to him. 

7. During trial one, State Defence lawyer was appointed to defend the absconding accused persons. 

8. The prosecution at the time of trial has examined as many as 17 witnesses including the informant Hajee Md Khorshed and the learned Magistrate, who recorded the confessional statement of the convict Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique. 

9. After the close of evidence from the side of the prosecution since only the condemned-convict Shafique was present in the accused-dock and the other two accused were absconding, he was examined under section 342 of the. Code of Criminal Procedure and at that time the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique pleading him not guilty declined to adduce evidence and claimed to be tried. 

10. From the trend of cross-examination of the witnesses and examination of the condemned-convict Shafique under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure the case of the defence is such that the accused are innocent and in no way connected with the killing of the deceased Atiqur Rahman @ Atique. 

11. After trial of the sessions case the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Sylhet considering the evidence and materials on record as well as facts and circumstances of the case, finding the convict persons guilty, sentenced them under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. The condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique was sentenced to death and his other co-accused Sumon @ Mama Sumon and Khokon (all along absconding) was sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life with fine of Taka 10,000 (Ten thousand) each, in default to payment of fine, to suffer additional imprisonment of two months each. 

12. Out of the said judgment and order of conviction and sentence this Death Reference No.78 of 2014 has been sent for the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman and for the other convicted person Sumon @ Mama Sumon Criminal Appeal No.3378 of 2015 was preferred against the judgment and order of conviction and sentence against him. 

13. With regard to the Death Reference as well as Criminal Appeal No. 3378 of 2015 Mr. Md Aminul Islam, the learned Deputy Attorney General with Ms. Shamsun-nahar (Laizu) and Ms. Farhana Afroze, the learned Assistant Attorney Generals appeared on behalf of the State. While Mrs. Hasna Begum was appointed state defence lawyer for the absconding accused. 

14. Mr. Md Aminul Islam, the learned Deputy Attorney General (hereinafter DAG) submits that the FIR of the case was lodged on 30-11-2010 at 22-10 hours and the date of occurrence was 29-11-2010 and the time of occurrence was between 3-04 pm to 3-30 pm The place of occurrence was Hotel Anurag, 2nd Floor, Room No.322. The learned DAG further submits that after proper investigation of the case police submitted charge sheet under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code on 18-6-2011. The charge was framed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, on 11-9-2012 and out of 31 charge-sheeted witnesses, 17 witnesses were examined by the prosecution, those who have successfully proved the case of the prosecution beyond all reasonable doubt. There is an extra judicial confession, in this case and about this confession, the prosecution witness No. 2, 11, 12 and 13 testified before the Court. The learned DAG also submits that the principal accused of this case is the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique, who has confessed his guilt under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and clearly implicated the other co-accused of this case, as of his two accomplices in the occurrence of killing the victim Atiqur Rahman @ Atique. The learned DAG argued that the Managers of the hotel Anurag, the prosecution witness No.3 and 7 categorically in their testimony testified that they have seen the convict persons and the prosecution case was totally corroborated by the witnesses including the managers. The learned DAG submits that the investigating officers of the case had no necessity to produce any witness to identify the assailants through T.I. parade, since there is a clear(distinct) video footage of the accused persons which was in the close circuit camera of the Hotel Anurag and that video footage was seized by the investigating officer and preserved, from where it is apparent that the two accomplice of the principal accused Shafique were accompanied by Shafique at the time of occurrence. The learned DAG submits that, without any mental or physical torture, fear or threat after the apprehension the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique, when he (Shafique) wanted to confess his guilt, he was produced before the learned Magistrate, 1st Class and the learned Magistrate complying the provisions of law properly, recorded the confessional statement of the condemned-convict Shafique under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and it is from the confessional statement itself that for reflection, three hours’ time was given to the convict Shafique before his 164 statement and, as such, there is nothing to discard the confessional statement of the condemned-convict Shafique. The learned DAG lastly submits that the prosecution witness No.2 Alamgir, who is the driver of the deceased as well as the informant, is a very important witness of this case, who is competent enough to corroborate the prosecution case. The Assistant Manager of Hotel Anurag the witness No.3 is also an important witness and the witness Nos.2, 3 7 and 10 are the direct ocular witnesses, who has witnessed the convicted persons to leave the place of occurrence immediately after the occurrence. The witness No.11 of the prosecution is also an important witness, who has talked with the condemned-convict over telephone after the occurrence. The witness No.12 and 13 are the witnesses of extra-judicial confession and the inquest report of the deceased which was immediately after the occurrence at 16.45 hours of the date of occurrence, and has clearly corroborated the injuries which were found in the dead body of the deceased Atique. From the contents of this report it is crystal clear that, there is no subsequent embellishment and the FIR is very much consistent with the inquest report and postmortem report of the deceased, wherefrom it is clear that there was a distinct mark of strangulation and the link of the occurrence has been well proved from the evidences on record, and it is also well proved that it was a preplanned cool-blooded murder, since the rope which was used in tiding in the neck of the victim was brought by the assailant Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique prior to the occurrence from outside. The learned DAG in support of his contention has referred a decision of this Court reported in 55 DLR 116 and relying upon the said decision in his concluding submission submits that the prosecution has successfully discharged their onus of proof by sufficient competent tangible and credible evidence and it is also proved that, prior to the confession of the principal accused Shafique before the learned Magistrate, (PW 16, Mr Shahabuddin Masum) there was no torture, threat or provocation to him by anybody including the police and therefore, the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Sylhet should be upheld. 

15. As against the aforesaid argument, Mrs. Hasna Begum, the learned Advocate appearing as State Defence lawyer in support of the defence submits that, against the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique in the instant case there is no eye witness in support of the prosecution case and there is no TI parade by which the assailants of the occurrence were identified. The learned State Defence Advocate further submits that there is no pre-meditation of the condemned-convict Shafique prior to the occurrence and there are several contradictions among the witnesses, who were examined in support of the prosecution case. The learned State Defence counsel lastly submits that the confessional statement of the condemned-convict Shafique is not true and voluntary, and it was not properly recorded by the learned Magistrate and the driver of the informant namely Alamgir, who was examined as prosecution witness No.2 admittedly has no appointment letter and, as such, the evidence of the driver cannot be relied on and there is no paper relating to business relationship of the deceased with the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman Shafique and, as such, the Death Reference is liable to be rejected. 

16. In respect of the Criminal Appeal filed on behalf of the convict-appellant Sumon Mama Sumon, none appeared to make any submission at the time of hearing despite; the matter has been posted in the daily cause list of this bench for days together with name of the learned Advocate for the appellant. 

17. In view of the argument advanced from both the sides, let us now scan the evidence adduced from the side of the prosecution and cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses including other evidence of this case. In the instant case, prosecution have examined as many as 17 witnesses including the Doctor, who did the postmortem of the dead body and the learned Magistrate, who recorded the confessional statement of the condemned-convict Shafique under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

18. PW 1 of the prosecution is the informant of this case Hajee Md Khorshed Ali. This witness in his testimony testifies that he is the informant of this case and proprietor of the place of occurrence Hotel Anurag. This witness also testifies that the victim Atiqur Rahman @ Atique happens to be his son and he was killed brutally. This witness in support of his ejahar corroborated the same in his deposition and at a stage categorically testified that after the occurrence the accused Shafique and his two accomplices while were leaving the hotel, the hotel Manager Salahuddin and Shahabuddin finding the accused asked them, as to where they are going and in reply, the accused Shafique told that they are going to SA Paribahan for bringing money. The informant of this case in his testimony identified his signature in the ejahar and clearly testifies that the ejahar was written and typed according to his statement and going through the ejahar he put his signature therein. He has identified the ejahar and his signature therein which has been marked as Exhibit-'1' and '1/1' respectively. The informant in his deposition also testified that the accused Shafique was arrested by the members of Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) on 15-2-2011 from Dhaka, who confessed his guilt after that, before a Judicial Magistrate under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The informant has identified the condemned-convict Shafique who was present then in the accused-dock. He also identified the co-accused Sumon who was also present at that time. The informant in his testimony testified at a stage that the video picture which was within the Close Circuit Camera of his hotel go to show that the accused Shafique, Khokon and Sumon came to his hotel and left his (PW 1) hotel after the occurrence and the video footage of the Close Circuit Camera was seized by the investigating authority in his presence and he put his signature in the seizure list. The informant identified the seizure list and the signature therein which have been marked as Exhibit-2 and 2/1 respectively. 

19. During cross-examination the informant in a reply to a question from the side of the defence admitted that his son Atiqur Rahman used to purchase CD and VCD from the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique and he (PW 1) has heard from his driver Alamgir that Atikur Rahman at the time of returning to his residence, was called on by the accused Shafique through mobile phone and getting that mobile call Atique returned back to the hotel and went to the room No.322, which was allotted in the name of the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman Shafique and its number is 322. The informant specifically denied that the accused Shafique because of torture after his arrest gave his confessional statement. 

20. PW 2 of the prosecution, Md Alamgir is a driver by profession and he testified before the Court during his testimony that he is the driver of the informant's private car and the date of occurrence is on 29-11-2010. On that date he brought the victim Atiqur Rahman at about 9-00 am to his hotel Anurag and at about 2-45 pm. Atiqur Rahman started to return back to his residence from hotel and when they reached to a place namely `Nayarpar' nearer to 'Fortune Garden Hotel', Atiqur Rahman received a phone call and with regard to this PW 2 testifies as follows: 
“আমি শুনি যে, আতিকুর রহমান বলেন তুমি কোথায়। উহার পর আতিকুর, রহমান গাড়ী ঘুড়াইয়া আমাকে হোটেলে যাইতে বলে। হইা দুপুরে খাওয়ার সময় বলিয়া আমি হোটেলে
ফিরিয়া যাওয়ার কারণ জানতে চাইলে আতিকুর রহমান বলেন যে, শফিক তাহাকে ফোন করিয়াছে। উহার পর গাড়ী নিয়া হোটেলে ফিরিয়া গেলে আতিকুর রহমান গাড়ী হইতে নামিয়া হোটেলের ভিতরে যায়৷ অনুমান ১৮/২০ মিনিট পর শফিক অপর দুইজন লোক সহ হোটেল হইতে বাহির হইয়া যায়। উহার অনুমান ৫ (পাঁচ) মিনিট পর জি,এম, জুয়েল সাহেবকে বলি যে, আতিক সাহেব শফিকের ফোন পাইয়া হোটেলের ভিতরে গেল কিন্তু শফিককে তো দুইজন লোকসহ বাহির হইয়া যাইতে দেখিলাম কিন্তু আতিকুর রহমান সাহেব তো আসিতেছেন না।”

21. This prosecution witness No.2 Alamgir in the last portion of his examination-in-chief testifies that after the arrest of Shafique, he (PW 2) has seen him (Shafique) in the RAB camp, where Shafique made a confession that he along with Sumon and Khokon has killed Atiqur Rahman. 

22. During cross-examination the witness No.2 testified at a stage that at the time of their returning back to the hotel, he asked the victim Atique, who has called him over phone. This witness in his testimony corroborated the prosecution case and denied the suggestion of the defence that he did not enquire into the caller of the phone, who over mobile phone called on Atique. This witness also denied that the accused Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique did not give any phone call to the victim, telling him to come back to the hotel. He also denied that the accused Shafique did not confess his guilt before the RAB. 

23. PW 3 Shahabuddin is the Assistant Manager of Hotel Anurag. This witness in his testimony testified that, prior to one year of the occurrence he joined in his post and the date of occurrence is 29-11-2010. On that date he was on duty from 3-00 pm and 3/5 minutes prior to that, he found Atiqur Rahman to start for his residence, but after 4/5 minutes Atique again come back to the hotel and went to the 2nd floor, and about 15/20 minutes to that, this witness observed that one boarder of that hotel 'Shafique' along with two others coming out of his room and going outside of the hotel, at which this witness asked him (Shafique) as to whether he will leave or come back to the hotel and in reply to that question, Shafique told him that for bringing money from S.A. Paribahan he is going outside and he wanted to know the location of S.A. Paribahan office from this PW 3. This witness also in his testimony testified that their General Manager Mahmuduzzaman @ Jewel after 10/15 minutes, coming before him informed that the mobile phone of their junior boss Atiqur Rahman is stopped, and stating that, their GM Mahmuduzzaman Jewel started to find out Atique and going in front of room No.322 hearing the sound of shower inside that room on bringing duplicate key, opened that room and same times after that, they informed this witness that their junior boss has been killed. Thereafter, PW 3 went to the place of occurrence room and found Atique fastened with the 'sofa' of that room, tide up neck, waist, hands, legs by rope and the mouth was closed by scotch tape. Finding that occurrence, this witness informed their senior boss over telephone and the GM of the hotel informed the police station and RAB through phone. At a stage of deposition, this PW 3 testifies that, hearing about the arrest of accused Shafique by RAB, they went to the office of RAB and in front of all, Shafique confessed that he along with Sumon and Khokon has killed their junior boss. 

24. During cross-examination PW 3 testified at a stage that he has deposed before the police officer sitting in the hotel, but he cannot recollect that date. PW 3 denied the suggestion that he did not tell anything before the Investigating Officer about his statement in the court.

25. PW 4 Md Abdul Monim is a seizure list witness. This witness testified before the Court that the date of occurrence is 29-11-2010 and at about 4.09 pm he has heard that Atiqur Rahman has been killed in hotel Anurag. In presence of this witness on 1-12-2010 the Investigating Officer from the ground floor of hotel Anurag within office room of the hotel seized the name and address of the assailant, which was written in the hotel register. This witness identified the seizure list and his signature therein which has been marked as Exhibit-3 and 3/1 respectively. 

26. During cross-examination PW 4 testified at a stage that Atiqur Rahman was his friend. 

27. PW 5 Abul Hasan Babul in his testimony testified that the informant Khorshed Ali happens to be his maternal uncle and the victim Atiqur Rahman is his brother. On 29-11-2010 the occurrence was held and in presence of this witness, the police officer prepared the inquest report of the victim Atique. This witness as witness of the inquest report put his signature. He identified the inquest report and his signature therein which has been marked as Exhdibit-4 and 4/1 respectively. This witness also testified that he has heard about the occurrence that in the boarder's room No.322 of the hotel, accused Shafique along with his accomplices committed the killing and after killing the deceased Atique, they have left the hotel at about 3-00/3-30 pm and the two other accomplices of the killer Shafique were Sumon and Khokon. 

28. PW 6 Mahmuduzzaman @ Jewel is the General Manager of Hotel Anurag and in his testimony he has testified about the case of the prosecution and corroborated the ejahar with other prosecution witnesses Nos.2, 3, 4 and 5. During his deposition PW 6 the General Manager of the Hotel categorically testified that when he noticed that the mobile phone of their junior boss Atiqur Rahman is switched off, he started searching and at a stage of that, he went in front of room No.322 and heard water falling sound from the closed room No.322 which is under lock and key from outside. Thereafter, bringing duplicate key of that room he opened the room and found their junior boss fastened by a rope with a 'sofa set' and his hands, legs, waist and neck tied up by that rope and the mouth of the deceased Atique was closed by a scotch tape. Finding that scenario this witness told the driver to inform the owner of the hotel instantly and he informed the RAB and police about the occurrence. After getting his information police and RAB came to the place of occurrence. During his deposition this witness No.6 Jewel testified at a stage that on 1-12-2010 from the office room of the hotel, investigating officer seized the bio-data of the boarder of the place of occurrence room No.322, the condemned-convict Shafique and in his (PW 6) presence the seizure list which was prepared for that seized alamat (papers), he put his signature. This witness identified the seizure list, his signature and the bio-data of the condemned-convict Shafique which were in two forms and marked as article Exhibit No. I and I/1 respectively. This witness also testified in his testimony that in the video of the CC Camera of that hotel it is found that the co-accused Khokon, and Sumon along with principal accused Shafiqur Rahman is entering into the hotel and going outside of the hotel and the police seized these videos through seizure list which were identified by this witness. 

29. During cross-examination this witness categorically testified at a stage that he has appointment letter about his appointment as General Manager of the hotel and his duty was in the hotel from morning to afternoon till 4-00 pm and thereafter, from 6-00/11-00 pm. This witness in a reply to a question from the side of the defence, specifically testified that at the time of occurrence the Managers were Salauddin and Sahabuddin, and they were on duty also. 

30. PW 7 Md Salauddin corroborated the witness No.6 and clearly testified before the trial court that he was on duty from 3-00 pm, and 20-25 minutes after his joining in the duty, he found the friend of their junior boss Atique namely Shafique and two others are going outside from the hotel. Finding them, this witness and his co-manager asked Shafique as to where they are going and in reply, Shafique told that they are going outside for bringing money from S.A. Paribahan. This witness in his testimony corroborated the prosecution case and also identified the accused Shafique in the accused-dock. 

31. PW 8 Moloy Dutta Mithu is a hearsay witness of this case. This witness has heard about the occurrence and in his presence the inquest report was prepared. As witness of the inquest report he gave his signature therein and besides this; in his presence the material exhibits i.e. the rope, the tiger drink bottle, the bad-sheet, scotch tape, CD cover, one under-vest and two bags were seized by police. The sofa set was also seized and a seizure list was prepared and as witness this P.W.8 gave his signature therein. 

32. PW 9 Sumon Chakraborty is another inquest report witness. This witness in his testimony testified that the deceased Atiqur Rahman Atique supervised the Hotel and on 29-11-2010 at about 3-00 pm while he was on duty in the nearby Chinese Restaurant belonging to the same owner, the informant of this case, at about 3-30 pm the General Manager of Hotel Anurag with other staffs went to his (PW 9) restaurant for searching their junior boss Atique. Hearing about the occurrence, thereafter this witness went to the place of occurrence and in his presence the inquest report of the dead body was prepared by police. 

33. PW 10 Shamsul Islam is a hotel boy of Hotel Anurag. This witness testified in his testimony that, since 2004 he is serving as hotel boy in the hotel and Atiqur Rahman @ Atique was their junior boss and the condemned-convict Shafique was known to him (this witness) since he(Shafique) came to their hotel frequently prior to the occurrence. PW 10 also testified that, 5/6 days prior to the occurrence, Shafique coming to their hotel became the boarder of room No.322, and on 29-11-2010 two guest of Shafique came to his room and stayed there till afternoon and at about 3.30 p.m. all the three accused jointly came out of the room and went outside, and subsequent to that, finding their junior boss no where they started searching and went to the 2nd floor of the hotel and in front of room No.322 they have heard sound of water falling and the room is under lock and key from outside. Thereafter, by duplicate key opening the door of the room they found their junior boss Atique, but his waist, hands, legs and neck were tide by a rope and the body was fastened with the sofa-set and his mouth was also closed by scotch tape and Atique was senseless and sent to Osmani Medical College Hospital, wherefrom the doctor told that he is dead. 

34. During cross-examination the PW 10 hotel boy Shamsul Islam testified at a stage that in the 2nd floor there are 25 rooms and 3 hotel boys were on duty at that time and Mizan was one of them. 

35. PW 11 of this case, Md Badrul Islam in his deposition testified that the victim Atiqur Rahman @ Atique happens to be his cousin's husband. On the date of occurrence at about 4-00 pm the father of the victim Khorshed Mia informed him that Atique has been killed and knowing about that, this witness rushed to the place of occurrence Hotel Anurag and found the body of the deceased Atique fastened with rope with a sofa-set tiding the hands, neck, waist and legs by that rope and the mouth is closed by a scotch tape. Atique was sent to Osmani Medical College Hospital wherefrom the doctor declared him dead and from 9-00/9-30 pm when this witness was in the residence of Atique, at about 1-00/1-30 a.m., a phone call came from a person which was attended by this witness, and at that time, that person disclosing him as a friend of Atique inquired about Atique as to whether he is alive and that number was '017-2520-6307'. This witness tried to know the identity of the caller but the caller disconnected the phone. Thereafter, this witness gave the number of that phone to everybody including the members of RAB and police and one hotel boy informed that the accused Shafique use that phone number and that number was given by Shafique to that hotel boy 2/3 time to flexi load. This witness also testified at a stage that after apprehension of Shafique he confessed his guilt in killing the victim before RAB, reporters and all of them and Shafique also disclosed the names of his accomplices namely Sumon and Khokon. 

36. PW 12 Most Rejia Begum is the mother of victim Atique. She has corroborated her husband, the informant of this case Hajee Md Khorshed Ali and also deposed that in their presence the accused Shafique disclosed before RAB that he along with Sumon and Khokon killed the victim Atique for want of money. 

37. PW 13 Tahmina Rahman is the wife of victim Atiqur Rahman Atique. She also corroborated the other witnesses and testified about the extra judicial confession by the condemned-convict Shafique before RAB and reporters. 

38. PW 14 is Doctor Abul Monsur. This witness in his testimony testified that he held the postmortem of the dead body of Atiqur Rahman Atique and during his examination he found the following injuries: "Complete circular ligature in the mid-level of neck found. Circular Ligature mark on both wrists joint which was found abraded in right wrist. Ligature mark on both forelegs found. Marks of contusion on the both lips found. Incisor teethes of both jaw found displaced." About the cause of death the doctor gave his opinion in the following way, "Considering autopsy findings and the inquest report, I am with the opinion that, the death of Atiqur Rahman Atiq was due to violent Asphyxia, resulting from strangulation, which was ante-mortem and Homicidal in nature". This witness identified the postmortem report and his signature therein which have been marked as Exhibit-6 and 6/1 respectively. 

39. PW 15 Sub-Inspector Abdul Alim is the 2nd investigating officer of this case. This witness testified in support of his investigation and clearly testifies at a stage that his previous investigating officer Sub-Inspector Khasrul Alam Badal due to his transfer handed over the case docket for investigation to him on 4-2-2011 and taking investigation of this case he went to the place of occurrence and seized the video footage of Close Circuit Camera of the place of occurrence hotel, the duplicate key of the place of occurrence room, the wearing apparels of the victim and prepared seizure list. This witness identified the seizure list and his signature therein which has been marked as Exhibit-7 and 7/1 respectively. This witness also testified that during his investigation he examined the witnesses and recorded their statements and the accused Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique confessed his guilt and this witness produced him before a learned Magistrate for recording his confessional statement. Thereafter, while the charge was proved against all the three accused-persons, this witness submitted charge-sheet against Shafique, Surnon and Khokon under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. The PW 15 also testified that his previous IO Khashrul Alam during his investigation seized some 'alamats' of the case i.e. the rope made of jute, the bloodstained handkerchief, the bed-sheet, the bloodstain undervest, the pillow cover, scotch tape, different CD and VCD through seizure list and also seized the mobile number '01752063087'.

40. PW 16 is a Magistrate, 1st Class, Md Shahabuddin Masum. This witness in his testimony testified that on 15-2-2011 as Senior Judicial Magistrate he was working at Sylhet and recorded the confessional statement of the accused Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and he has complied with the provisions laid down in section 164 and 364 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and after observing all the legal formalities he has filled up the HCB form 'M-84'. This witness identified the confessional statement and six signatures which have been marked as Exhibit-11 and 11 /1-11/6. The learned Magistrate also testified that the confessional statement was read over and explained to the accused person and admitting that true and voluntary, the accused gave his three signatures therein. 

41. During cross-examination from the side of defence the witness No.16, the learned Magistrate categorically testified before the trial court that three hours’ time was given to the accused for his reflection and he was in his court chamber for that time and he (PW 16) observed the accused Shafique but did not find any mark of injury or violence in his person and the learned Magistrate also assured the accused that he will not send back to police and he will be sent to the jail custody. This witness denied the suggestion of the defence that the confession is the product of torture by police. 

42. The last witness of this case, the witness No.17 is the 1st investigation officer, Sub-inspector Khashrul Alam Badol. This witness in his testimony testified that during his investigation he went to the place of occurrence and prepared the sketch map, index etc. and also prepared the inquest report of the dead body and seized the alamats including 46 cubits long rope, one bloodstained handkerchief, one bed-sheet, one undervest, two pillow covers and a scotch tape through a seizure list. He also seized some VCD, an old bag, and one royal tiger drinks plastic bottle. This witness identified the seizure list and signature therein and also identified the materials, which were seized by him during his investigation and all these material exhibits have been marked as material Exhibits-II series. 

43. On meticulous consideration of the evidences on record along with the case record and scanning the material exhibits including the medical examination report, FIR, inquest report and the confessional statement of the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman Shafique, it transpires that the series of evidences as adduced from the side of the prosecution, has corroborated one another as to the link of this case and the learned Magistrate who recorded the confessional statement of the principal accused the condemned-convict Shafique, during recording of the statement strictly complied with the provisions laid down in section 164 and 364 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and it was clearly explained to the accused before recording of his confessional statement that, (i) the learned Magistrate is not an officer of police but a Magistrate; (ii) that he is not bound to make a confession; (iii) that if does make a confession it may be used in evidence against him; (iv) that he should not say anything because others have told him to say it but is at liberty to say whatever he really desires to say; (v) that he should say nothing which is untrue. 

44. Apart from this, there is a clear declaration of the learned Magistrate to the effect that the confession was voluntarily made and it is true. In this context; in the case of ABM Nazmus Sakib Ashik vs State, 12 BLC (AD) 203; our Apex Court held, the Magistrate appears to have recorded his satisfaction as to the voluntariness and spontaneous nature of the confession of the accused. It appears that the confession has not been vitiated by any illegality. Besides, this Court in the case of Abut Hossain vs State, 46 DLR 77; opined that the provisions under sections 164 and 364 of the Code of Criminal Procedure are mandatory and required to be strictly followed to make the confession voluntary and true and fit for reliance for convicting the accused on his confession. In the case of Nausher Ali Sarder vs The State, 39 DLR (AD) 194; their lordships held that the surrounding circumstances are ordinarily the only material from which the inference of a confession may be drawn. Confession when proved against the confessing accused, it can be taken into consideration against co-accused in the same offence. 

45. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and the discussions referred to above, we are constrained to hold such a view that here in this case it is proved beyond all shadow of doubt by series of cogent evidence that the condemned-convict Shafique is directly involved with the offence of killing the victim Atiqur Rahman Atique. We also find that the learned trial court in fact during examination of the convicted-appellant Suman mama Suman under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure complied with the provisions by giving attention of the accused to the incriminating evidences which were produced against him and, as such, no illegality or irregularity is noticed by which it can be held that the convicted persons have been prejudiced or has been deprived of getting justice from the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Sylhet. 

46. Furthermore, obviously we have every reason to draw such inference that there was no ambiguity or confusion in the mind of the accused before giving reply to the question put before him by the learned trial court and in view of the facts and circumstances of the case we are of the considered view that the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Sylhet during deciding the fate of the case in favour of the prosecution committed no such infirmity by dint of which the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence of death can be interfered with. Moreover, it is observed that the learned trial court rightly considered the case in its true perspective. 

47. Having gone through the evidences on record we find on our anxious consideration over the testimonies of the ocular witnesses, who personally witnessed the convicted persons immediately after the occurrence at the time of their leaving the place of occurrence hotel and being satisfied on the assessment of the evidences by the trial court in its total approach, we are inclined to hold such a view that the trial court committed no wrong. Moreover, the ingredients of the offence as we have spelt out were also duly appreciated by the learned trial court and, as such, in the discussions made above particularly the nature of the offence and the confession of the principal accused as to the implication and participation of the convicts in the heinous crime of killing the victim Atiqur Rahman Atique, we are of the view that the prosecution has been able to prove the case beyond all shadow of doubt and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence should be sustained. 

48. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case it is crystal clear from the factual aspects, that the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique with the previous intention to murder the victim Atiqur Rahman Atique which was pre-meditative, under the ambit of section 300 of the Penal Code committed the murder. As such we find nothing in the circumstances of the case and the conduct of the condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman to take lenient view in the matter of sentence despite our best concern to temper justice with mercy. Considering all aspect of the matter we are obliged to the law to sustain the order of conviction and sentence. 

49. Before parting, however, we must observe that the circumstantial evidences which are evident from the face of the records are cogent and despite in the instant case there is no direct eye witness of the occurrence, the circumstantial evidence as it appears is trustworthy, tangible and credible, and hence, it cannot be ignored and definitely the circumstances makes it clear that the absconding condemned-convict and his accomplices the appellant Sumon @ Mama Sumon and Khokon are directly involved in the occurrence of killing the victim Atique and under section 8 of the Evidence Act, 1872 the abscondence of the condemned-convict and Sumon after misusing the bail privilege being on guilty conscience, is a strong corroboration to the prosecution case that they are the culprits. The extra judicial confession which is transpires from the testimony of the witnesses, are also a corroboration of the prosecution case as well as the confession made by the confessing condemned-convict Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique. 

50. Be that as it may, we are inclined to hold such a conclusion that the argument advanced from the side of the learned Deputy Attorney-General Mr Md Aminul Islam is consistent with the case record and, as such, these are well founded. 

51. In the result, the Death Reference No.78 of 2014 is accepted and consequently, the Criminal Appeal No.3378 of 2015 be dismissed. The impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence dated 12-11-2014 awarded by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Sylhet in Sessions Case No.1808 of 2013 (previous Sessions Case No.736 of 2012) is hereby upheld and confirmed. 

52. Let the Death Sentence of the condemned-convict namely Md Shafiqur Rahman @ Shafique (absconding), son of Hazi Rahmat Ullah, 28 Ganaktuli Lane, Police Station-Hazaribag, Dhaka, be executed after his arrest/surrender in accordance with law and the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Sylhet in Sessions Case No.1808 of 2013 (previous Sessions Case No.736 of 2012) in respect of the remaining convict-appellant Sumon @ mama Sumon is affirmed. 

Send down the lower Court's records along with the copy of this judgment to the court concerned at once for information and necessary action. 

End.
